beats.vo: A calendar date is not a claim that the month paid you. Last page you wrote that leverage is not part of the paper plan. This lesson puts a date on the reread, and it refuses to treat the date as a result. On the diagram for this beat, look for a calendar chip with a results box crossed out beside it. The shapes are the lesson. If a shape is only decoration, it does not belong on this frame. Draw this month's box and cross out any result line inside it. Mark the page Example, so a later reader cannot mistake the sketch for a recommendation to trade an asset or these levels. A date cannot prove that a grid paid you. Say the opening line once more, and point at the part that belongs to Hook. If you cannot point yet, do not move on. The point of the beat is the pointing.

By the end you can set a review cadence that does not assume a gain. The cadence opens the same four words: band, spacing, inventory, stop. It does not open a profit figure. Write the four words as the whole card. Mark the page Example, so a later reader cannot mistake the sketch for a recommendation to trade an asset or these levels. Adding a result row because the card looks empty is the miss. Say the opening line once more, and point at the part that belongs to A cadence without a gain. If you cannot point yet, do not move on. The point of the beat is the pointing.

One approach is a monthly read of the same page: band, spacing, inventory, and stop. You read what you wrote. You do not add a new line because the month turned. On the diagram for this beat, look for the same notebook opened on a new month, the four lines unchanged until a written change. The shapes are the lesson. If a shape is only decoration, it does not belong on this frame. Copy last month's four lines, then decide if any word is now false. Mark the page Example, so a later reader cannot mistake the sketch for a recommendation to trade an asset or these levels. A new month is not itself a reason to add size. Say the opening line once more, and point at the part that belongs to One approach. If you cannot point yet, do not move on. The point of the beat is the pointing.

A change is a new written line, not a habit of adding. If the band, the step, the inventory, or the stop is now wrong, you write the new sentence and you cross out the old one. On the diagram for this beat, look for one line crossed out and a new line under it, stamped Example. The shapes are the lesson. If a shape is only decoration, it does not belong on this frame. Practice one crossed-out line and its replacement. Mark the page Example, so a later reader cannot mistake the sketch for a recommendation to trade an asset or these levels. Adding without crossing out hides which plan you are on. Say the opening line once more, and point at the part that belongs to A change is a new line. If you cannot point yet, do not move on. The point of the beat is the pointing.

If your old notes say to add the result back, cross that sentence out. Mark the page Example, so a later reader cannot mistake the sketch for a recommendation to trade an asset or these levels. The disclaimer sits here because the old version wrapped a rate around a hope. Say the opening line once more, and point at the part that belongs to Old frames. If you cannot point yet, do not move on. The point of the beat is the pointing.
